output.summary: A deciduous shrub or small tree native to eastern Asia from the Himalayas to Japan, autumn olive readily colonizes barren land and is invasive in parts of the United States and Europe. It often has sharp thorns, while its leaves emerge silvery and become greener above through summer. The ripe red, silver- or brown-dotted berries are sweet-tart and may be eaten fresh or made into jam, condiments or flavouring.
output.edibilityNote: Ripe red berries are eaten fresh or processed into jam, condiments or flavouring; they have a sweet-tart taste.
